welcome.label: Welcome · the silent camera

parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: The Silent Camera
parts.body: What caught the moths in the dark, and how did it find them?

welcome.script:
Welcome back, scientists! The case isn’t over. Dr. Reyes put one more camera by the pond.

[ON SCREEN: 9:41 PM · 9:52 PM]
At 9:41, moths are flying around the porch light. Eleven minutes later, they’re gone, and the camera saw nothing move. Hmm.

[ON SCREEN: The printout]
But her bat detector heard something at that exact minute. Look: slow clicks, faster clicks, then a buzz. I wonder what that means.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
That’s our case. Find four clues today. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · echo hunt (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🔊 Echo
parts.title: What’s an echo?
parts.body: A sound that bounces off something and comes back.

warmup.script:
(Clap once, then pretend to listen.) If I clap near a wall, the sound bounces back. That’s an echo.

[ON SCREEN: Echo]
Bats use echoes to hunt. A bat clicks, and the echo off a moth comes back to its ears.

[ON SCREEN: Test click]
In the echo hunt, press Click and read how long the echo took. A quicker echo means a closer moth. Use the test click to help you, then drag the pin to the moth. Find it three times.

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes first.

vocab.label: Word Wall
vocab.script:
[ON SCREEN: Pathway]
A pathway is the path a message follows: stimulus, sense organ, brain, response. (Trace four steps in the air.)

[ON SCREEN: Model]
A model shows how something works. Today you build pathway models.

Tap each word below me to hear it.

part1.label: Part 1 · build a strong model (Clue 2)

parts.label: ✅ A strong model
parts.title: What makes a model strong
rows: “Signal” on the arrow to the brain
A caption about a survival need

part1.script:
[ON SCREEN: The bonneted bat]
Meet our suspect: the Florida bonneted bat, Florida’s biggest bat. Look at those ears!

[ON SCREEN: A strong model]
A strong model has four things: the four steps in order, an arrow between each step, the word signal on the arrow to the brain, and a caption about a survival need.

Build one for the bat in the game below. Watch the meter fill up as your model gets stronger.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

figure.label: The eagle and bat picture
figure.script:
[ON SCREEN: Two pathways]
Read this picture like two sentences. Top row, the eagle: a fish flashes, the eye sees it, a signal goes to the brain, the eagle dives. Bottom row, the bat. Point to each step. Which step looks the most different?

part3.label: Part 3 · match the sense (Clue 3)
part3.script:
[ON SCREEN: Match]
Four Florida animals, four different senses. Read what each one notices, then drag in the sense organ that can pick it up. When all four are done, look across. What stayed the same? Press Listen first.

explore.label: Part 4 · fix the broken models (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🛠 Broken model
parts.title: A volunteer drew:
parts.body: An echo bounces off a moth → The bat grabs the moth

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: Broken model]
One of the volunteers drew this. An echo bounces off a moth, and the bat grabs it. (Count on your fingers: one, two.) Hmm, only two steps. I notice something’s missing.

[ON SCREEN: Run it]
In Part 4, pick what’s wrong, drag in the missing step, then press Run the model and watch the signal go all the way through. There are three broken models: the bat, the eagle and the bear.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What happened at the pond?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You made it to the assignment! First, crack the case at the top. Still locked? Tap “Show me where the clues are.” Pick the answer that fits every clue.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then three parts. Part B: two short answers. Part C: build two pathway models for two Florida animals that use different senses, then compare them. A sketch is a bonus. And last, your CER.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

partc.label: Part C · two pathway models
partc.script:
[ON SCREEN: Two models]
Pick two Florida animals that use different senses, not the bat or the eagle. Maybe an owl that hears and a snake that smells? Write the four steps for each, then tell how they’re alike and different.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The quote
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “You only need to build one pathway model to understand how all animals respond. Building two is a waste of time.”

parts.label: ⚖ CER
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Claim: what you think is true.
Evidence: facts from the lesson that prove it.
Reasoning: how the facts prove your claim.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The quote]
A classmate says one model is enough to understand every animal. Hmm.

Think back. Would a bat model tell you how a bear finds berries? Or how a crab feels the water?

[ON SCREEN: CER]
Pick your side in the planner, tap two pieces of evidence, then write your reasoning in your own words. Try starting with “This shows that…”

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🦇 Your specimen
parts.title: Bat detector printout
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next week
parts.title: Like parent, like child
parts.body: How do Florida plants and animals pass their traits to their young?

closing.script:
[ON SCREEN: Confetti]
Case closed! A bat clicked, its ears caught the echoes, and its brain worked out where the moths were. Same four steps as the eagle, just a different sense.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Check every box in What to Turn In, and the bat detector printout goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Next week]
Next week: families! Why do baby animals look like their parents?

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

vr.label: VR activity · Twin pathways (separate page)

parts.label: 🖊 The dive slate
parts.title: The water smudged it
parts.body: Dr. Reyes sketched a dolphin and a hammerhead shark on her dive slate. Rebuild both pathway models side by side.

parts.label: 🧭 Two ways
parts.title: Two ways to do it
rows: VR Field Mission: two lanes under the sea (Under The Ocean) that end at one model brain.
No headset? Build a manatee lane and a scrub-jay lane, then sort same or different.

parts.label: 🥈 The badge
parts.title: Silver Sonar Wave badge
parts.body: Save your capture in VR to earn it.

vr.script:
Hi, scientists! Dr. Reyes saw a dolphin hunt with echoes, just like our bat!

[ON SCREEN: The dive slate]
She sketched it next to a hammerhead shark, but the water smudged her slate. Rebuild both pathway models, side by side.

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]
Pick your way at the top. With a headset, go under the ocean and build two lanes that end at one model brain. Say each lane’s four steps out loud.

[ON SCREEN: The manatee lane]
No headset? Build a lane for this manatee and one for a scrub-jay. What is the same? What is different?

[ON SCREEN: The badge]
Finish in VR and you earn the Silver Sonar Wave badge!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.
